expectations.text: Cites Art. 31(12): financial entities may only use a third-country-established CTPP if it establishes an EU subsidiary within 12 months of designation
expectations.evidence: Cites Art. 31(12)+12-month subsidiary but inverts the mechanism: frames it as a provider-only duty ('not a direct financial-entity obligation', 'not a new obligation created for you'), contradicting the use-restriction on financial entities.

expectations.text: Applies the dates: designation November 18, 2025 (first CTPP list, 19 providers including major cloud/SaaS) → the subsidiary must exist by ~November 2026
expectations.evidence: 'published by the ESAs... on 18 November 2025 (19 providers...)' -> 'deadline at approximately 18 November 2026'

expectations.text: Draws the consequence: without the EU subsidiary, continued use becomes non-compliant — verify the provider's subsidiary status now
expectations.evidence: Advises 'Verify subsidiary status directly with the vendor' but denies the non-compliance consequence: 'this is not a new obligation created for you, but a vendor-compliance deadline... a leading indicator', never states continued use becomes non-compliant.

expectations.text: Recommends contingency: exit strategy (Art. 28(8)) readiness and substitutability/concentration analysis (Art. 29)
expectations.evidence: 'Confirm your exit strategy is current and testable' and 'Re-run your Art. 29 concentration-risk assessment' (exit strategy miscited as Art. 28(7), substance present).

expectations.text: Places it in the oversight framework: Lead Overseer and Joint Examination Teams are running the first full oversight cycle in 2026
expectations.evidence: '2026 is the first full oversight cycle for the CTPP framework; JETs (Joint Examination Teams...) are conducting initial examinations' with Lead Overseer powers described.
